candidate.subject: english
candidate.body: According to paragraph 1, what do smartphone notifications do to the people in the room?

options.text: Repeatedly draw their attention away from conversations
Help them listen more closely to others
Make their time pass more slowly
Prevent them from looking at screens

candidate.explanation: Paragraph 1 expressly describes notifications interrupting conversations and attracting attention to screens. A: Directly restates both effects in the passage. B: Closer listening contradicts interrupted conversations. C: No slowing of time is claimed. D: Attention is drawn towards screens, not prevented from reaching them.
candidate.passage_text:
(1) A room is filled with people whose faces glow in the light of their smartphones. Moments drift away like autumn leaves in the wind. Notifications repeatedly interrupt conversations and draw fingers towards screens.

(2) When phones are out of reach, people feel anxious and incomplete. The writer compares this feeling to a phantom limb: an absent digital device seems like a missing part of oneself. Fear of missing out drives repeated checking.

(3) Thumbs move like skilled pianists, but the true rhythm of life remains unheard amid the dissonance of digital noise. Constant connectivity creates a hunch on shoulders, a physical sign of the burden of information overload. Minds stay alert for the next like, share or comment.

(4) Despite efforts to stay connected, people become increasingly isolated among digital faces. Genuine connections are fleeting amid the constant clamour for attention. The search for digital validation sacrifices meaningful moments and shared experiences.

(5) The writer urges readers to value presence and engagement in moments that matter. What defines people is the depth of their connections and the richness of their experiences, rather than their number of likes or followers.

learning_objective.objective: Answer a direct comprehension question about one paragraph of a passage.
learning_objective.why_answer_requires_it: The student must read paragraph 1 to find what the notifications do.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: For a hypothetical budget, total receipts other than borrowings are ₹27.2 lakh crore and total expenditure is ₹45 lakh crore. Which deficit equals ₹16.8 lakh crore?

options.text: Revenue deficit
Fiscal deficit
Budgetary deficit
Primary deficit

candidate.explanation: Fiscal deficit subtracts receipts excluding borrowing from total expenditure. 45 − 27.2 = 17.8 lakh crore. Revenue and primary deficits require different supplied quantities. A: Revenue deficit uses revenue expenditure and revenue receipts; neither pair is supplied. B: Matches expenditure minus receipts excluding borrowings. C: This is not the named NCERT fiscal-deficit identity. D: Primary deficit also removes interest payments, which are not supplied.

oracle.basis: 45 minus 27.2 equals 17.8, not the displayed 16.8; the numerical premise is false.

candidate.subject: accountancy
candidate.body:
In each independent case, a new partner brings a cash premium for goodwill, and the existing partners sacrifice part of their shares. Match each situation in List-I with its accounting treatment in List-II.

List-I
(A) The new partner pays the premium directly and privately to the existing partners.
(B) The premium is received through the firm and initially credited to Premium for Goodwill A/c.
(C) The premium is received through the firm and initially credited to the new partner’s capital account before distribution to the sacrificing partners.
(D) The premium has been credited to the existing partners’ capital accounts in their sacrificing ratio, and they retain the amount in the business.

List-II
(I) No entry is passed in the firm’s books.
(II) Bank A/c Dr. to Premium for Goodwill A/c; then Goodwill A/c Dr. to the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts individually.
(III) Bank A/c Dr. to the new partner’s capital account; then the new partner’s capital account Dr. to the sacrificing partners’ capital accounts individually.
(IV) No additional entry is passed for retaining the credited amounts in the business.

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
candidate.explanation: A premium paid directly and privately to the existing partners requires no entry in the firm’s books. When the premium is received through the firm, the entries depend on whether it is credited initially to Premium for Goodwill A/c or to the new partner’s capital account. If the credited amounts are retained in the business, no additional entry is passed.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Unit II: Reconstitution of a Partnership firm
learning_objective.objective: Match goodwill-premium situations on the admission of a partner with their accounting treatment.
learning_objective.why_answer_requires_it: The student must know how each way of receiving a goodwill premium is recorded.

oracle.basis: Receiving a premium credits Premium for Goodwill; distributing it must debit that same account. Debiting Goodwill leaves the received premium uncleared. The worked example confirms the clearing entry.

candidate.subject: economics
candidate.body: A government records two receipts. The first is a tax receipt and the second is a non-tax receipt. Neither receipt leads to a claim on the government. How should these receipts be classified?

options.text: Both are revenue receipts: one is tax revenue and the other is non-tax revenue.
Only the tax receipt is a revenue receipt; the non-tax receipt is a capital receipt.
Only the non-tax receipt is a revenue receipt; the tax receipt is a capital receipt.
Neither receipt is a revenue receipt because neither leads to a claim on the government.

candidate.explanation: A receipt that does not lead to a claim on the government is a revenue receipt. Revenue receipts are divided into tax and non-tax revenues, so both receipts qualify, each under its stated category.

learning_objective.syllabus_unit: Course II Unit IV: Government Budget and the Economy
learning_objective.objective: Classify government receipts as revenue or capital receipts.
learning_objective.why_answer_requires_it: The student must know the test that separates revenue receipts from capital receipts.

oracle.basis: Non-tax sale of a government asset creates no repayment claim but reduces assets and is a capital receipt. The stem does not exclude this counterexample; its universal revenue-receipt explanation is insufficient.

candidate.subject: business_studies
candidate.body: An automobile company divides work into production, purchase, marketing, accounts and personnel. Which of the following is a disadvantage of this organisation structure?

options.text: It may lead to an increase in cost.
Managers may gain power, assert independence and ignore organisational interests.
It ensures that different functions get due attention.
Heads do not get training for top management positions.

candidate.explanation: Dividing work into production, purchase, marketing, accounts and personnel departments forms a functional structure. NCERT lists among its disadvantages that functional heads do not get training for top management positions because they cannot gather experience in diverse areas. Ensuring that different functions get due attention is an advantage of this structure.

learning_objective.objective: Identify a disadvantage of a given organisation structure.
learning_objective.why_answer_requires_it: The student must recognise the structure from its departments and recall its listed disadvantages.

oracle.basis: Both independent reviewers found the item contestable: the same functional-structure excerpt describes functional empires and departmental interests being pursued at the cost of organisational interests, so option B overlaps a functional-structure disadvantage while being worded like the divisional-structure one; the second reviewer also found option A defensible on a loose reading. The official key and the textbook-category key is D. Retained as a natural multiple-defensible defect (key shown is the official D).

source_custody.subject: business_studies
source_custody.hold_basis: broad_alternative_overlap_requires_second_independent_review_before_truth_label | second: Options A and B are generic or divisional-structure disadvantages; a loose reading of A (cost increase) could be defended by some students, though it contradicts the functional-structure advantage of lower cost.
